title_guess: National income and GDP: what a product is (goods and services), GDP as the year's value of final goods and services made inside the country, and six GDP rules with small examples
recurring_cast: person icons (Ram in blue, Shyam in purple; later a seller and a buyer)
country_flag row (four countries) over an INCOME / NATIONAL INCOME band
NATIONAL INCOME tag with the GDP, NDP, GNP, NNP list
price_tag with ₹ (₹10 on goods, ₹5 on services)
two yellow boxes 'aggregate of all goods / services produced in a financial year' feeding ₹ + ₹ = GDP
india_map with GDP written on it, fed by an arrow from the boxes
cyan rule list on the left (Indian company in India, foreign company in India, exchanged for money, final goods) that grows one row per rule
step_tracker: six numbered blocks at the bottom, the current rule's block raised
factory icons (spice maker with smoke, steel maker, automotive, tools fabricator)
laptop with a 10K price, passed between people
running_examples: Ram earns 10K a month, Shyam 2 lakh a month (transcript reads 2,000)
ketchup: tomatoes -> factory -> bottle; goods ₹10, services ₹5
spice maker: 100 packets at ₹5; 80 sold (₹400 counted), 12 left in the godown, 8 taken home
steel -> automotive (10 cars sold) and tools fabricator (5 tools sold); steel is intermediate
1 kg steel sold at ₹5; fabricator adds ₹10; tool sells at ₹15; the ₹5 is already inside the ₹15
old laptop bought for 10K sold on a resale site for 5K: no GDP effect
shopkeeper buys a laptop for 10K and sells it for 15K: GDP effect? (left to the comments)

best_moments.why: the person-income band (Ram, Shyam) turns into a band of country flags and the label becomes NATIONAL INCOME: a country's income is shown as the same idea as a person's, scaled up
a three-step strip (pile of tomatoes as raw materials -> machine line -> ketchup bottle) and the bottle is boxed as GOODS: 'finished good' is seen being made
goods and services boxes each drop a ₹ through a down arrow into one sum bar '₹ + ₹ = GDP', with India's map standing beside: GDP as the money value of two piles added
a numbered step tracker (1-6) appears at the bottom and a cyan rule list grows on the left as each rule is done: the learner always sees which rule of six is on

100 spice packets split into three branches; only the 'sold in market' branch climbs to the GDP map with a tick, the godown and self-use branches are crossed: inclusion shown as which line reaches GDP (the rule itself is doubtful)

1 kg steel at ₹5 goes to the tools fabricator, '₹5 + ₹10' is written over it, the tool sells at ₹15, and an 'already included' bracket runs from the steel's ₹5 to the ₹15: double counting made visible in numbers
a resale loop (seller -> laptop 10K -> resale site -> buyer, 5K back) inside a band whose line to GDP is crossed: 'no new production, no GDP' as a blocked path

weak_moments.why: doubtful rule drawn as fact: unsold stock left in the godown and goods taken home for own use are crossed out of GDP, while national accounts count stock added to inventories and own-account production of goods

the statistics office logo is linked to GDP with a ministry name around it; the office named was merged into a new national statistics office in 2019, the ministry name and the office-holder said aloud need checking
real software brand logos (and later a real insurer's web page, a spice brand, a steel brand and a resale website) carry the examples; BIE uses generic ones
the caption says 'final goods and services' about 3 minutes before final goods are taught

the spice-packet scene starts right after a 17 s stretch with no recognised speech (260-277 s) and the ₹400 sum falls in another 13 s gap; the picture carries 100, 80, 12, 8 and ₹5 while the voice is lost
screen shows Shyam at 2 lakh a month while the transcript reads 2,000; probably a recognition error, but a check should catch it
four measures (GDP, NDP, GNP, NNP) are named and spelled out but only GDP is taught; the other three hang as branches

segments.teaches: two people earn different monthly incomes; who earns more in a financial year? (Shyam)

elements.what: two standing persons, Ram (blue) and Shyam (purple)
INCOME band: Ram 10K/month, Shyam 2 lakhs/month
question text above: in one financial year who earned more?
'<' sign between them; box round Shyam's income

segments.notes: 5 change events. Screen 2 lakhs/month vs transcript 2,000 per month (likely recognition error). The answer and the bridge to countries fall in a 12 s transcript gap (16.5-28.3 s).
segments.idea: income is measured over a period; compare two people's yearly earnings
segments.shown_as: two person icons stand on an income band with their monthly figures; a question asks who earned more in a year, then a '<' sign pops between them and Shyam's figure is boxed

segments.teaches: every country also has an income in a year, its national income; it is measured in several ways, four of them GDP, NDP, GNP, NNP; GDP is the most stable (why: later)

elements.what: four country flags replacing the two persons, dashes in their income cells
band label changes from INCOME to NATIONAL INCOME
four lines from the label to GDP, NDP, GNP, NNP
green tick on GDP and a red handwritten 'why?'

segments.notes: 4 change events. The country cells hold only dashes: no figures.
segments.idea: a country's yearly income is national income, and it has four main measures
segments.shown_as: the two people give way to four country flags on the same band, whose label becomes NATIONAL INCOME; four lines branch down to GDP, NDP, GNP, NNP; GDP gets a tick and a scribbled 'why?'

segments.teaches: full forms: gross domestic product, net domestic product, gross national product, net national product; the common word is product

elements.what: NATIONAL INCOME tag at top left
four rows: abbreviation, dash, full form writing on one by one

segments.notes: 5 change events, each full form on its spoken word.
segments.shown_as: the canvas clears to a list; each measure's full form writes on as it is said

segments.teaches: a product is anything a company produces: ketchup, a flat, a sofa, software, a car, cooking oil

elements.what: 'Product' heading
ketchup bottle, apartment block, sofa, car, cooking oil bottle
two real software brand logos

segments.notes: 8 change events, each object on its word. Brand logos are named products of real firms.
segments.idea: products are physical things and also software, all made by someone
segments.shown_as: under a 'Product' heading a ketchup bottle appears, then a flat building and a sofa, then two software logos, then a car and an oil bottle in the same row; the row fades
segments.example: ketchup, flat, sofa, software, car, cooking oil

segments.teaches: a ketchup company turns raw tomatoes into a finished good in its production unit; finished goods are products

elements.what: pile of tomatoes (raw materials) -> machine line with red arrows -> ketchup bottle
black box round the bottle labelled GOODS
caption: raw material is converted into finished goods

segments.idea: a good is a finished thing made from raw materials
segments.shown_as: a strip runs from a heap of tomatoes through a machine line to a ketchup bottle; the bottle is boxed and labelled GOODS and a caption writes on under the strip

segments.teaches: services (banking, insurance, shipping) are products too; goods and services together are products, and each has a money value

elements.what: screenshot of a real insurer's web page listing its plans under 'Products', the list boxed and labelled SERVICES
GOODS box with the ketchup bottle and SERVICES box with 'banking, insurance, shipping'
price tags ₹10 on goods and ₹5 on services

segments.notes: 5 change events. The ₹10 and ₹5 tags are never spoken; the voice says only that you must pay.
segments.idea: a product is a good or a service, and anything you pay for has a money value
segments.shown_as: the boxed ketchup sits beside a real insurer's 'Products' page whose plan list is boxed as SERVICES; it settles into two boxes, GOODS and SERVICES, and a price tag swings onto each

segments.teaches: GDP is the total value of all goods plus all services produced in a financial year inside the country's geographical boundary; gross = total, domestic = inside the boundary; Indian and foreign companies producing in India both count

elements.what: India map at top right, pulsing when 'country' is said
the two boxes become 'aggregate of all goods / services produced in a financial year'
₹ from each box down into a bar: ₹ + ₹ = GDP
caption: many final goods and services are produced within India's geographical boundary; 'Domestic' handwritten under the highlighted boundary words
two cyan rows: Indian company producing goods in India; foreign company producing goods in India

segments.notes: 11 change events. The caption says 'final goods' before final goods are taught (364 s).
segments.idea: GDP adds up the money value of a year's goods and services made inside the country, whoever owns the firm
segments.shown_as: India's map appears beside the goods and services boxes, which turn into yearly aggregates; each drops a ₹ through an arrow into a sum bar that ends '= GDP'; the boundary words are highlighted and 'Domestic' is scribbled under them; the map pulses and two cyan rows (Indian firm, foreign firm, both in India) slide in at left

segments.teaches: recap: rules 1 and 2 (Indian or foreign company producing in India counts); a six-step tracker appears

elements.what: cyan rule rows -> aggregate boxes -> arrow -> GDP written on the India map
step tracker: six numbered blocks at the bottom; blocks 1 and 2 raised, then 3
red box round the two cyan rows

segments.notes: 5 change events. The tracker stays for the next five minutes.
segments.idea: two rules done out of six
segments.shown_as: the board recomposes into one line: rule rows, the two aggregate boxes and an arrow into a GDP-labelled India map; six numbered blocks rise at the bottom with the first two up, and the two rule rows are boxed

segments.teaches: rule 3 (as taught): only goods exchanged for money count: of 100 spice packets at ₹5, the 80 sold add ₹400; 12 left in the godown and 8 taken home are not counted

elements.what: factory with smoke and a spice brand's letters, arrow to a spice packet marked 5₹
'[100 packets]' splitting into three branches: 80 sold in market, 12 still in the godown, 8 used for self consumption
line from the 80 branch up to the GDP map with a green tick
red crosses on the lines from the 12 and 8 branches
'goods/services exchanged for money' over the 80 branch, then added as row 3 of the rule list

segments.notes: 9 change events. Transcript gaps at 260-277 s and 291.7-304.9 s, so 100 packets, ₹5 and the ₹400 total are mostly carried by the picture. Doubtful: change in inventories and own-account production of goods are counted in GDP.
segments.idea: as taught: a good enters GDP only if it is sold for money
segments.shown_as: a smoking factory sends out a ₹5 spice packet; '100 packets' splits into three branches (sold, godown, home); the sold branch draws a line up into the GDP map with a tick, the other two draw lines that are crossed in red; a 'exchanged for money' label joins the rule list
segments.example: 100 packets x ₹5; 80 sold = ₹400 counted; 12 unsold, 8 self-used not counted (as taught)

segments.teaches: rule 4: only final goods count; steel bought by car and tool makers is an intermediate good (an input to other goods) and is left out; the cars and tools sold are counted

elements.what: steel factory with a steel brand's name, arrow to STEEL
STEEL splitting to an automotive factory and a tools fabricator; outputs '10 cars sold' and '5 tools sold'
blue 'Final Goods' box round the cars and tools with a ticked arrow up to GDP
grey box over STEEL: intermediate goods [inputs for other goods]; 'not considered in GDP calculation' below
row 4 'Final Goods' added to the rule list

segments.notes: 10 change events. '10 cars sold' appears inside a 6.7 s transcript gap (357.8-364.5 s); the 10 and 5 counts are never spoken.
segments.idea: a good used up to make another good is intermediate and is not counted separately
segments.shown_as: a steel factory feeds STEEL, which branches to a car maker and a tool maker; '10 cars sold' and '5 tools sold' come out and are boxed in blue as Final Goods with a ticked arrow into GDP, while STEEL is boxed grey as an intermediate input and marked not counted
segments.example: 10 cars and 5 tools counted; steel not counted

segments.teaches: why intermediate goods are left out: 1 kg steel sold for ₹5 becomes a 1 kg tool; the maker adds ₹10 of costs and profit and sells it for ₹15; counting the steel's ₹5 as well would count it twice

elements.what: steel factory -> '1kg STEEL' -> tools fabricator -> '1kg' tool, '1 tools sold'
₹5 under the steel; '₹5 +' then '+ ₹10' over the fabricator; ₹15 beside the tool, boxed blue
bracket from the steel's ₹5 to the tool's ₹15 labelled 'already included'

segments.notes: 5 change events. The ₹15 and the 'already included' bracket appear inside a 14 s transcript gap (455.4-469.6 s); the spoken list of costs (labour, machinery, overheads, transport, profit) is not drawn.
segments.idea: a final price already contains the value of its inputs
segments.shown_as: 1 kg steel at ₹5 flows to the tool maker, who writes '₹5 + ₹10' over himself; a 1 kg tool sells for a boxed ₹15, and a bracket runs from the steel's ₹5 to that ₹15 marked 'already included'

segments.teaches: rule 5: selling an old laptop (bought for 10K) for 5K on a resale site adds nothing to GDP, because nothing new is produced; it was counted in the year it was made

elements.what: seller -> laptop 10K -> resale site logo -> buyer; 5K arrow back to the seller
red cross on the line from the blue band up to GDP
note: no goods or services produced here; already counted when produced

segments.idea: GDP counts this year's production, not resale of old goods
segments.shown_as: a seller hands a 10K laptop through a resale site to a buyer and 5K comes back along the bottom; the band's line up to GDP is crossed in red and a note explains

segments.teaches: rule 6, left as a question: a shopkeeper buys a laptop from a company for 10K and sells it to you for 15K; does this affect GDP? (answer in the comments, to come next video)

elements.what: laptop 10K -> shopkeeper at a counter -> buyer 15K
cluster of coloured question marks by the GDP map

segments.notes: 5 change events. No answer given; the trade margin is the point the learner must find.
segments.idea: does a shop's resale margin count in GDP? (open question)
segments.shown_as: a 10K laptop goes to a shopkeeper at a counter and on to a buyer with '15K' under him; coloured question marks pop beside the GDP map

segments.teaches: back to the four measures (GDP picked out); the national statistics office computes GDP

elements.what: NATIONAL INCOME list (GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP) with 'Product' underlined in each
box round the GDP row
statistics office logo with a ministry name round it, linked to the GDP box

segments.notes: 4 change events. The list order differs from the opening (GNP before NDP). Doubtful: office and ministry name (see weak moments).
segments.idea: GDP is one of four measures, and an official office calculates it
segments.shown_as: the opening list returns with 'Product' underlined in each row; the GDP row is boxed and a line runs to a statistics office logo
